summary: Mt. Hood NF lookout: 60-foot three-legged tower built 1919, removed 1967; the frame cabin stands, restored 2002, and an August 2026 closure notice applies.

facts.design: three-legged timber platform tower about 60 feet tall, with a frame living-quarters cabin
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1967; the frame living-quarters cabin still stands after a volunteer restoration project in 2002
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mount Hood National Forest)

access.note: Oregon Hikers field guide notice dated August 2026: the area is closed because of the Austin Fire; the Forest Service closure order governs

visit.trail_note: Out-and-back hike from the Rho Ridge Southern Trailhead to the cabin; the field guide describes the restored cabin as available to visitors on a first come, first serve basis

events.note: Three-legged platform tower erected with a frame cabin for living quarters
Site abandoned in the 1950s (registry and firelookout.com; no exact year given)
Inspection by F.R. Nelson, Collowash Ranger District: tower has no cab and is used in extreme fire conditions; living quarters in good condition
Three-legged tower removed; the cabin remained
Volunteers took on a restoration of the living-quarters cabin after it fell into disrepair; the field guide later calls the cabin restored
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register January 2, 2026; nominated by Danielle Sullivan
Oregon Hikers notice (August 2026): area closed due to activity from the Austin Fire; see the USFS closure order

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The firelookout.com page we read says the frame cabin is still there and does not describe the tower as standing. The registry and the Cheryl Hill page record the tower as removed in 1967. Recorded as gone, with the cabin standing.

The registry and firelookout.com say the site was abandoned in the 1950s. A 1963 inspection report describes the tower as used for extreme fire conditions and the living quarters as in good condition. The story reports both; the sources do not settle which is right.

notes_for_editor: Sources agree on the 1919 build, the 1967 tower removal, and the cabin that still stands. Elevation differs slightly: the registry gives 1,600 m and firelookout.com gives 5,277 ft; the record keeps the registry figure. The 1950s abandonment date conflicts with the 1963 inspection; both are kept. The access level 'closed' rests on an Oregon Hikers notice dated August 2026, so it may be stale; re-check the USFS closure order before publishing. The 'first come, first serve' cabin line is from the field guide, which also mentions spring 2016 trail conditions, so treat it as dated. A Mount Hood NF office contact would settle current access.
